problem:
John has $3$ pants, $5$ shirts, and $6$ pairs of socks.
If John wears one pair of pants, one shirt, and one matching pair of socks, how many different combinations of outfits can he wear?

feedback.problem: Magnus is ordering lunch. He wants to get a starter soup, a drink, a main dish, and a dessert. The menu has $8$ main dishes, $3$ soups, $10$ drinks, and $5$ desserts for him to choose from. How many choices does Magnus have to order a meal?
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the **rule of product**, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Number of possible meals} & =\text{Number of main dishes} \\  & \times \text{Number of soups} \\  & \times \text{Number of drinks} \\  & \times \text{Number of desserts} \\  & =8\times 3\times 10\times 5 \\  & =1\,200.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, Magnus has $1\,200$ choices to order a meal.
